record_type_quote: Coifman et al. (2021) found that major personal stressors exert stronger effects on psychological risk than work-related potentially traumatizing events in first responders. The current study sought to replicate and extend these findings by testing within-person effects of different stressor types on weekly sleep and risk behaviors, and by modeling how these micro-level processes shape long-term adjustment across the first year of college.
